title: HarborView Insights - prototype integration notes
content:
Meeting summary:
- Date: 2025-11-03 (45m) — kickoff call with HarborView Insights (HV).
- Attendees: Aisha T. (Redwood SE), Marco R. (Redwood infra), Lena P. (HV product), Harpreet S. (HV infra), Sana (HV data).

Business problem / ask:
- HV wants a prototype that adds semantic search + realtime summarization to their media-analytics dashboard. Primary user flow: ingest transcripts and metadata from live streams, surface relevant clips via search, and show one-paragraph AI summaries for clip previews.
- Timeline: prototype in 3 weeks, internal demo week 4. Production follow-up depends on cost/perf.

Hard constraints called out by HV:
- Data residency: US East only for prototype; long term must support customer-specified regions (APAC later).
- PII: transcripts may contain names/phone numbers; they need token-level redaction before indexing.
- Throughput target (proto): 100 search QPS peak, 20 summarizations/sec (latency target <= 750ms p50 for summarization).
- SLA: prototype can be best-effort; production expects predictable latency and dedicated capacity.
- Security: SSO for Console, KMS for key wrapping, audit logs for inference requests.

Notes on current HV infra:
- Ingest pipeline: Kafka topic per show -> preprocessor (removes fillers, timestamps) -> S3 long-term store + ElasticSearch for metadata.
- They currently run in GCP (us-east4) in a VPC with strict egress rules; on-prem not required.

Technical requirements we sketched:
1) Embeddings pipeline
   - Use Redwood API for initial prototype hosted or Dedicated depending on cost estimate.
   - Batch embedding job for historical corpus (approx 1.2M segments) — suggest using batch/sliced runs with concurrency 8, quantized model for cost savings.
   - For live segments, stream short texts to Redwood embeddings endpoint with a light L2 cache at application layer for duplicates.
   - Feature: add synthetic doc-level metadata (show_id, timestamp) to embedding payload so we can join later.
2) Semantic search stack
   - Index vectors into their existing ES or we recommend Milvus/Vector DB if ES can't scale vectors (HV wants to avoid another infra piece for prototype).
   - For proto use ES tiebreaker but watch performance at 100 QPS; plan fallback to Redwood dedicated routing if ES query latency becomes bottleneck.
3) Summarization generation
   - Chat-generation endpoint (streaming) for preview summaries.
   - Default model suggestion: redwood/medium-10B (placeholder) for quality; provide quantized 8-bit variant for Dedicated to reduce GPU memory.
   - Use prompt templates with extractive prefilter (shortest clip <= 3k tokens). For clips > 3k tokens we will chunk and use KV cache/prefix caching.
4) PII redaction
   - Two-layer approach: (a) local preprocessor regex + NER (spaCy) to remove obvious PII, (b) Redwood hosted-inference step with a small classification model to detect residual PII; redact before storing embeddings or sending to summarization.
   - Need explicit acceptance from HV legal for any model-in-the-loop redaction on production data (log/telemetry controls).
5) Security & compliance
   - Key management: integrate HV KMS via Redwood Private key-wrap or supply Customer-Managed Key for Dedicated.
   - Audit logs: require request-id propagation to join logs across systems; ensure Console can surface per-request token and model info.
   - Network: for Private or Dedicated, will need static egress IPs or VPC peering options to comply with HV firewall rules.

Performance / cost estimates (rough)
- Embeddings batch job (1.2M segments, avg 250 tokens): with 8-concurrency quantized runner => ~12–18 hours and ~$Xk estimate (TBC).
- Live embeddings: 100 QPS * avg 1.5 calls/sec per user peak -> capacity needs 100 concurrent embedding requests; recommend Dedicated pool of 2x GPU inference pods (model/quantization dependent).
- Summaries: target 20/sec, p50 <= 750ms. For redwood/medium-10B quantized, expect p50 ~ 400–600ms on A100-like instance.

Gotchas & open issues (must resolve before prototype kickoff)
- HV's ElasticSearch vector indexing currently uses dense_vector field type but isn't optimized; at 100 QPS similarity lookups may hit CPU bounds. Need to measure.
- PII policy: HV legal wants explicit clause that Redwood doesn't persist raw transcript data for hosted models — discuss Private or Dedicated to satisfy.
- Tokenization mismatch: HV text preprocessor does some custom normalization (emojis, timestamps). Need alignment on exact text used for embeddings vs summaries to avoid drift.
- Model fallback behavior: HV wants deterministic fallback — if Dedicated capacity saturated, requests should route to a smaller cheaper model and degrade gracefully (no hard errors). Need to design routing policy and customer-visible SLOs.
- Monitoring: HV asks for per-request cost breakdown in Console for demo; we can show estimated token counts but may need a sample dashboard layout.

Prototype implementation plan (3-week sprint)
- Week 0 (this week): finalize scope + confirm data sharing for sample corpus (1 week of transcripts). Owner: Lena.
- Week 1: integrate embeddings pipeline (batch job + live path), wire HV test ES index, run perf smoke tests. Owner: Marco + HV infra.
- Week 2: add summarization endpoint integration, prompt tuning for 10 sample shows, PII redaction loop. Owner: Aisha + HV data.
- Week 3: end-to-end demo, fix perf regressions, prepare short runbook for next steps (Dedicated sizing / private deployment). Owner: Aisha.

Action items (owners + due dates)
- HV: provide sample dataset (2–3 shows, ~5k segments) by 2025-11-06. Owner: Lena P.
- Redwood infra: produce rough Dedicated cost estimate matrix (embeddings per 1M, gen tokens per 100k) by 2025-11-05. Owner: Marco R.
- Redwood SE: prepare prompt templates and two summarization examples (long and short) by 2025-11-07. Owner: Aisha T.
- Legal: draft data handling note for HV (hosted vs dedicated implications) by 2025-11-10. Owner: Harpreet S. (HV Legal contact) + Redwood Legal (TBD).

Notes-to-self / internal reminders:
- For prototype, prefer Hosted API to accelerate iteration unless HV insists on KMS/private; include cost guardrails in demo to avoid surprise bills.
- Build a small script to canonicalize transcripts (timecode removal, emoji normalization) — include inverse mapping so summaries can show timecodes.
- Verify ES similarity query latencies with synthetic load (100 QPS, top-k=10) before demo.

Potential follow-ups for production proposal:
- Dedicated capacity with autoscale + warm pools to hit <200ms p50 for summaries.
- KV cache usage for repeated viewers to reduce per-token cost.
- Long-term vector DB recommendation (managed Milvus or Pinecone) if HV wants high QPS with low tail latency.

End of notes.
